items.item_text: Able to travel to support field work.
Job offer is contingent upon satisfactory clearance based on Background Check results.
Must be willing to work with hazardous materials.
Occasional overtime and weekends may be required.
Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent experience) in chemistry, microbiology, environmental science/engineering, or a related field.
Hands-on laboratory experience with aseptic technique and handling biological samples.
Experience in fieldwork, including carrying equipment and working outdoors in variable conditions

The Prather Research Lab at Scripps Institution of Oceanography is seeking a motivated Laboratory Research Assistant to support ongoing research into aerosol production, composition, and the airborne transmission of microbial pathogens. This position plays a critical role in advancing two major interdisciplinary research initiatives: CAICE, which investigates how aerosol particles influence climate, air quality, and atmospheric chemistry, and the Airborne Institute, which studies the intersection of climate change and airborne disease transmission while developing practical solutions to improve air quality indoors and outdoors.

The Lab Assistant will work at the intersection of atmospheric chemistry, environmental microbiology, and field science, contributing to a research program that uses both laboratory-based aerosol generation systems (including novel "ocean-atmosphere" simulation chambers) and real-world field sampling to understand how aerosols form, travel, and impact human health and the environment.

This is a hands-on, laboratory- and field-based role suited to someone early in their scientific career who is eager to gain direct experience in aerosol science, bioaerosol sampling, and environmental microbiology, while working alongside a highly collaborative, interdisciplinary team of scientists, postdoctoral researchers, and graduate students.
Ability to follow biosafety protocols and work with biohazardous material.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Proven ability to successfully work on multiple concurrent projects.
Strong record-keeping skills (sample logs, SOPs, lab notebooks).
